correctness.rationale: For Gauss E(1/N), every irrational survivor has regular CF digits >=N; the countable inverse IFS x->1/(a+x) is uniformly contracting and satisfies OSC. Its pressure is bounded by logs of the Hurwitz sums V_N and U_N, yielding zeta-root enclosure. At upper root U_N=1, 1-V_N <=2/N^2, and |V_N’| >= log N throughout the root interval, proving width <=2/(N^2 log N). Uniform first Euler–Maclaurin expansion and derivative estimates locate the root at 1/2+W(log N)/(2log N)+W(log N)^2/[4N(log N)^2(1+W(log N))] + O(1/(N^2 log N)). Squeeze by N=floor(1/alpha) gives leading law for all alpha↓0. Code tests finite scalar consequences only.

originality.rationale: Direct 2026 source arxiv:2610.14534v1 proves the qualitative Gauss survivor dimension jump, pressure characterization and minimum-digit coding, but relevant full-text Sections 4–5 and main results do not derive the Lambert-W scale, lattice correction or finite-N explicit zeta-root enclosure. Chitu–Sebe–Lascu arxiv:2603.27635v1 (Theorem 1.2; Remarks 1.3–1.4) compares strongly: for the ordinary Gauss case its classic Good-type inequalities only bracket dimension between 1/2+1/(2log(N+2)) and 1/2+loglog(N-1)/(2log(N-1)). Those cannot imply the lower logloglog refinement or first lattice correction. Fang–Moreira–Zhang arxiv:2409.00521v1 concerns growing digits at specially selected positions, not a uniform cutoff N at every time. published-finding corpus and accessible own claim searches yielded no implication, though search absence alone is not novelty proof. Historical lower-cutoff theory remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Quantifies the natural abrupt Hausdorff-dimension change at zero Gauss hole size, resolving both the slow Lambert-W leading scale and the first discrete Euler–Maclaurin finite alphabet effect. A rigorously quantified Hurwitz root enclosure isolates map-specific distortion below that resolved correction, unlike known broad Good-type inequalities. This supports reliable study of dimension sensitivity in countable-branch open dynamics, without falsely claiming a global spectrum or exact root equality.
